# Asymmetric Embedding Configuration

LightRAG keeps embedding behavior symmetric by default. Query/document asymmetric
embedding is enabled only when `EMBEDDING_ASYMMETRIC=true` is explicitly set.

Do not reuse an existing vector store across asymmetric embedding configuration
changes. Mixing vectors generated with different query/document behavior can
make retrieval quality unpredictable.

## 1. 适用场景与策略选择

### 1.1 P 策略要解决什么问题

The P strategy is valid for the structured output of **any parser that can produce a `.blocks.jsonl` sidecar** (`native` / `mineru` / `docling`) — all three persist an identically-structured `.blocks.jsonl` (carrying `heading` / `level` / `parent_headings`) through the shared `write_sidecar()`. Only the `legacy` engine produces no sidecar; input without a sidecar (the legacy path or a parse failure) automatically degrades to the R strategy (see §6).

Semantic Router supports local embedding models through the `LocalEncoder` class. This integration allows you to generate embeddings entirely on your machine using sentence-transformers, with no API keys or internet connection required.

## Overview

The `LocalEncoder` provides access to open-source embedding models from sentence-transformers. All computation happens locally on your CPU, CUDA GPU, or Apple Silicon (MPS), making it ideal for privacy-sensitive applications or offline deployments.

description: IndexedRouter, DecisionRouter, Chain and Merge, and how to build your own router.

A router takes a query, scores every route, and hands back a decision. Version 1 has several kinds of router, and they all share one contract: each scores the routes its own way, and the base class does the rest. Thresholds, calibration, evaluation, sync and async calling, and adding and removing routes all work the same on every router.
